en.name: John Vianney
en.summary: The "Cure of Ars," a French parish priest famed for hearing confessions up to sixteen hours a day.
en.body: John Vianney struggled academically, particularly with Latin, and was ordained only after his superiors judged his holiness sufficient to compensate for his weak scholarship. Assigned in 1818 to the obscure rural parish of Ars, he transformed it through relentless preaching, personal austerity, and above all his confessional ministry, spending up to sixteen hours a day hearing confessions as pilgrims began arriving from across France, drawn by his reputation for spiritual insight and reports of supernatural harassment by the devil. He is said to have heard the confessions of tens of thousands of people in his final years alone. He died in 1859 and was declared patron saint of parish priests by Pope Pius XI.
